He said: 'A loaf.' The Jew said: 'Fine white bread, by my father, you are!' The Prophet, may Allah's peace and blessings be upon him, laughed, then said: 'May Allah fight the Jews! Do you know what dirmaka is? It is the essence of bread.'"

The report that the earth on the Day of Resurrection will be one loaf, which the Mighty One will turn over in His hand as one of you turns over his loaf while traveling, as a provision for the people of Paradise, has already been mentioned. It is in the two Sahihs, from the narration of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, traced to the Messenger of Allah, may Allah's peace and blessings be upon him.

Some have related that the change occurs in the earth, but it is changed for each group according to its condition: one group of believers will be on bread from which they eat, another group will be on silver, and the group of disbelievers will be on fire. Changing it into anything whatsoever is not greater than creating it after it did not exist.

Some have mentioned that its attributes are changed first, in the manner narrated from Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, and then its essence is changed, and this latter will be after its news has been told. There is no barrier to there being various changes here.

In Sahih Muslim, from the hadith of Aisha, may Allah be pleased with her, traced to the Prophet: "People on the Day when [the earth] is changed will be on the Sirat." And in it, from the hadith of Thawban: "A Jew asked the Messenger of Allah, may Allah's peace and blessings be upon him: 'Where will people be on the Day the earth is changed into another earth?' He, peace be upon him, said: 'They will be in darkness, short of the Bridge.'" Perhaps what is meant by this change is a particular kind of it. And Allah, exalted is He, knows best the reality of the matter. The mention of the changing of the earth first is because it is closer to us, and because its changing is a greater matter in relation to us.

﴿And they will come forth﴾, meaning: the creatures, or the wrongdoers, who are indicated by the context, as was said. What is meant by their coming forth is from their graves which are in the depths of the earth.

It was permitted that what is meant is their appearing with their deeds, which they used to do secretly and thought would not be disclosed, or that they act like one who thinks so. The reason the coming forth is attributed to them, even though according to this it belongs to their deeds, is that it indicates they will take forms suited to those deeds. You know that the apparent meaning is their coming forth from their graves, and the connection is to ﴿is changed﴾, and the shift to the past tense form is to indicate the certainty of its occurrence.

Abu al-Baqa' permitted that the sentence be a new (resumptive) sentence, or that it be a circumstantial clause (hal) from "the earth," with an implied verb meaning "lies sleeping," and the connecting element being the waw.

Zayd ibn Ali, may Allah be pleased with them both, read (wa-buzzirū) with a damma on the ba' and a kasra on the ra', doubled, making it passive, in the sense of multiplicity relative to the object, because of the large number of those brought out. ﴿To Allah﴾, meaning: to His judgment, glorified is He, and His recompense, ﴿the One﴾, who has no partner, ﴿the Subduer﴾, ﴿(48)﴾ the Victor over everything. The mention of the two attributes is to magnify the gravity of the affair and to inspire awe, because when they stand before a great, subduing King who has no one sharing His rule, they will be in peril, since none can withstand Him and there is no helper other than Him. And in that there is also confirmation of the arrival of the promised punishment, on the assumption that ﴿the day the earth is changed﴾ is a substitute for ﴿the day the punishment comes to them﴾.

[Page 256]

"﴿And you see the criminals﴾" is coordinated with "﴿they came forth﴾" (*'ataf*, coordination). The shift to the present-tense form serves either to bring the scene vividly before the mind (*istihdar al-surah*) or to indicate continuity (*al-istimrar*). Coming forth, however, is a sudden event with no continuity. If "they came forth" is taken as a circumstantial clause (*hal*), then "﴿and you see the criminals﴾" is coordinated with "﴿is replaced﴾." It has also been permitted to coordinate it with the governing element of the preceding adverbial phrase, on the assumption that it is something like "it will bring about": "﴿on that day﴾," meaning the day when they came forth before God Most High, or the day when the earth is replaced, or the day when His promise is fulfilled. If "seeing" (*al-ru'yah*) is visual, then "the criminals" is its object, and "﴿bound together﴾" is its circumstantial qualifier. If it is cognitive, then "the criminals" is its first object and "﴿bound together﴾" its second.

The meaning is that some of them are bound together with others, each joined to his companion in his disbelief and his deeds, like the verse "﴿and when souls are paired﴾," according to one opinion. There is also the proverb: "Birds of a feather flock together." Or they are bound together with the devils who led them astray, like the verse "﴿So by your Lord, We will surely gather them and the devils﴾," etc. Or they are bound together with the corrupt beliefs, the wicked dispositions, and the evil deeds they committed, once these are given form and shape in accordance with them, in the frightful forms and terrifying shapes. Or they are bound together with the recompense for these things, or with the record of them. In that case there is no need for the notion of their deeds taking on forms. Or their hands and feet are bound to their necks. This has come in some reports, and the apparent meaning is that it is literal.

It is also possible, as has been said, that this is a figurative representation (*tamthil*) of their being held to account for what their hands and feet committed. The root of *muqarran*, with the doubled letter, is one who is gathered in a *qaran*, with the vowel on the letter *qaf* and the letter *ra* unvowelled, which is the cord by which something is tied. "﴿In fetters﴾" (49). *Al-asfad* is the plural of *safad*. It is also pronounced *sifad*, and it denotes the shackle placed on the leg, or the iron ring worn on the hand and neck, or that which joins the hand and foot to the neck, which is called *jami'ah*. From this is the saying of Salamah ibn Jandal:

"Zayd al-Khayl has met with shackles,
biting on forearm and on shinbone."

It is also transmitted as *safada* with a light pronunciation and *saffada* with a doubled letter for intensity. You say *asfadtuhu* when you give him something, so with the *hamzah* in this sense. It has been said that *saffada* and *asfada* are both used for binding and for giving, and gift is called *safad* because it binds:

"And whoever finds kindness a fetter is bound by it."

The prepositional phrase is connected either to "﴿bound together﴾" or to an elided element that stands as a circumstantial qualifier from its pronoun, i.e., "shackled." Abu Hayyan permitted that it stands in the position of a qualifier (*sifah*) of "﴿bound together﴾."

Commentary of al-Alusi (Ruh al-Ma'ani) on surah 14, verse 50:

﴿Their garments﴾ — i.e., their shirts; the plural of sirbal. ﴿Of tar﴾ — it is what is extracted from the abhal tree (Pinus/juniper-type tree), then boiled, and with it mangy camels are daubed, so it burns the mange because of its intense sharpness, and its heat may reach the interior. It is black and foul-smelling, and fire kindles in it quickly, to the point that it has been said: it is the swiftest of things to catch fire. In al-Tadhkira it is mentioned that it is of two kinds: a thick, glossy, sharp-smelling kind, known as al-barqi, and a thin, liquid kind, known as al-sa'il. The first is from the Shirbin specifically, and the second is from rice, sidr (lote tree) and the like. The first is better. It is hot and dry in the third or second degree. It is mentioned regarding zift (pitch) that it comes from trees such as the cedar and others, and that if it flows by itself it is called zift, while if it is produced by craft it is qatran. It is also said: qattan, on the pattern of sakran.

It is narrated from Umar and Ali, may Allah be pleased with them both, that they recited it as ﴿wa-qutran﴾ on the pattern of sarhan, but we have not found anyone who recited it thus. The sentence of subject and predicate is in the position of an accusative as a circumstantial clause (hal) from al-mujrimin, or from their pronoun in ﴿muqarranin﴾, or from ﴿muqarranin﴾ itself, according to what has been said; its link is only the pronoun, as in the phrase "fuwahun ila fi" (a mouth to a mouth), or it is a resumptive (independent) sentence. Whichever it is, in ﴿their garments﴾ there is an eloquent simile (tashbih baligh), for the intended meaning is that the skins of the people of the Fire are smeared with tar until its coating becomes like garments. It seems that this is so that four kinds of torment gather upon them: its sting, its burning, the speed of the fire in their skins, the horrifying color, and the stench.

Yet the disparity between that tar and what we witness is like the disparity between the two fires; so what we witness of them are the names of their named realities in the Hereafter. By His abundant generosity we seek refuge, and under His wide protection we take shelter. It is also permitted that there be in the speech a metaphorical allegory (isti'ara tamthiliyya), by likening the soul clothed in bad qualities, such as disbelief, ignorance, obstinacy and dullness, to a person who has put on garments of pitch and tar. The point of resemblance is that each of them is adorned with a foul, harmful matter to its possessor, which is abhorred when seen, and the name of one is borrowed for the other. The shortcoming of directing the allegorical metaphor in this way is not hidden, and it is evident. Moreover, the claim of this metaphor here is the closest thing possible to the speech of the Sufis.

Some have said: It is possible that the tar mentioned is the very thing they clung to in this life and made their emblem: false beliefs and evil deeds that draw down every kind of punishment, which have taken bodily form in the next life in that shape, entailing the intensification of punishment. May Allah Most High protect us from that by His kindness and generosity. You know that the eloquent simile on this view remains as it is.

Ali, may Allah ennoble his face, and Ibn Abbas, Abu Hurayra, Ikrima, Qatada and a group recited ﴿min qatirin aan﴾, taking them as two words, both nunated: the first is qatir, with a fatha on the qaf and a kasra on the ta', which is copper in general or what has been melted from it; and the second is an, on the pattern of 'an, meaning of extreme heat.

al-Hasan said: Jahannam has been kindled over it since it was created, so its heat has reached its end. ﴿And the Fire covers their faces﴾. (50) That is, the Fire that is kindled by their bodies clothed in tar covers them and surrounds them. The specifying of the faces with the stated ruling, along with its generality for all their other limbs, is because they are the most honored and noblest of the visible limbs, as in His saying, Most High: ﴿Is one who shields his face from the evil of the torment on the Day of Resurrection [like one who is secure]?﴾ And because they are the gathering place of the senses and faculties, which they did not use for what they were created for, namely perceiving the truth and reflecting upon it. This is like the statement that it "looks upon their hearts," because the heart is the noblest of the inner organs and the locus of knowledge, and they have filled it with ignorances; or because it is free of tar, as it is said, so that the fire's covering of it is not mentioned. The reason for leaving it free of that is perhaps that they may recognize one another when the flame occasionally uncovers them, and that their punishment is doubled by disgrace before the assembled witnesses.

It is also read with the faces in the nominative and ﴿the Fire﴾ in the accusative, as if he made the arrival of the faces at the Fire a figurative covering of it. It is also read ﴿taghsha﴾, meaning tatagashsha, with one of the two taas elided. The sentence, as Abu al-Baqa said, is in the accusative as a circumstantial clause, like the preceding sentence.

In al-Kashf: Al-Allama al-Tibi stated that "muqarranin," "their garments are of tar," and "taghsha" are circumstantial clauses from the object of "tara" (you see), placed in this sequence for ascending order. For this reason the second was made a nominal sentence, because the garments of tar, gathering the four kinds (of torment), are more dreadful than the chains. As for "taghsha," it is for renewing the presence intended in His saying, "wa-tara" (and you see), because the second is more terrifying. It is apparent that the second and third are detached from the ruling of seeing, because the first describes their state at the place of standing until they are cast into the Fire, and the last two describe their state after entering it. It seems that the first stirred in the listener the question: if this is their condition at the place of standing, how then will they be in Jahannam, where they abide forever? So He answered with His saying, Glorified is He: ﴿Their garments are of tar﴾. The verb in the present tense was chosen for the second, to present the state and the renewal of the covering moment by moment. Most of the grammarians hold that they are not detached.

Commentary of al-Alusi (Ruh al-Ma'ani) on surah 14, verse 51:

﴿Liyajziya Allah﴾ (so that Allah may recompense) is connected to an implied verb, meaning: "It is done to them thus, so that He, glory be to Him, may recompense ﴿every soul﴾," i.e., every criminal soul, by the indication of the context, ﴿for what it earned﴾ of the kinds of disbelief and sins, a fitting recompense. In this there is an announcement that their recompense is commensurate with their deeds. It is also permitted, on this reading, that "soul" be more general, including both the criminal and the obedient, because when only the criminals are singled out for punishment, the singling out of the obedient for reward is known, along with the fact that the punishment of the criminals, who are their enemies, is also a recompense for them, as it is said:

Whoever lives a day after his enemy has reached his desire.

It is also permitted, on the consideration of generality, that the lam be connected to "they came forth" (barazu), on the assumption that it is coordinated with ﴿is changed﴾, with the pronoun referring to the creation, and what lies between them is a parenthetical clause, "there is no obstruction." That is: they came forth for the reckoning, so that Allah, exalted is He, may recompense every soul, obedient or disobedient, for what it earned of good or evil. ﴿Indeed Allah is swift in reckoning﴾. (51) Because He, glory be to Him, is not occupied by examining and tracing it, and no reckoning prevents Him from another reckoning, so that some of them would rest while He is busy calling the others to account, and thus the punishment would be delayed for them. It is narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, that what is meant is "swift in retribution." Al-Murtada, in his Durar, mentioned other interpretations of this.

This is a message (bala gh): that is, what was mentioned from His words, glory be to Him, ﴿And do not think that God is unaware of what the wrongdoers do﴾ up to here. It is also permissible that the reference is to the Qur'an, which is narrated from Ibn Zayd, or to the surah, with the masculine form used in accordance with the predicate, which is "a message." The first view is more eloquent, as if it were said: "This that has been mentioned just now is sufficient as admonition and reminder, without need for what the noble surah contains, or the whole glorious Qur'an, of the various kinds of admonitions and calamities." The root meaning of *balagh* is a verbal noun in the sense of *tabligh* (conveying), and al-Raghib (al-Isfahani) explained it in this way in the verse. He also mentioned its use in the sense of sufficiency in another verse: ﴿This is a message for mankind﴾, specifically for the disbelievers, on the assumption that the warning is restricted to them in His words, glory be to Him: ﴿And warn mankind﴾; or for them and for the believers together, on the assumption that it includes them as well, even though what was explained is specific to the wrongdoers, as it is said. ﴿And that they may be warned by it﴾ is a conjunction with something omitted, meaning "that they may be advised," or "that they may be warned by it," or something similar; so the *lam* is connected to *balagh*. It is also permissible that it be connected to an omitted element, and its estimate is "and that they may be warned by it, it was sent down," or "it was recited." Al-Mawardi said: the *waw* is superfluous. From al-Mubarrad: it is the conjunction of a singular with a singular, meaning "This is a message and a warning." Perhaps this is an explanation of meaning rather than of grammatical analysis. Ibn Atiyya said: meaning "This is a message for mankind, and it is for that they may be warned by it," so that is made a predicate of an omitted *huwa*. It is also said that the *lam* is the *lam* of command. Some of them said: this is good, were it not for His words, glory be to Him: ﴿and that they may remember﴾, for it is in the accusative case only. Abu Hayyan approved of this and said: what was mentioned does not undermine it, since it is not required that ﴿and that they may remember﴾ be conjoined to the imperative, but rather a verb may be implied for it, to which it is connected. It is not hidden that this is a forced interpretation.

Yahya ibn Imara al-Dharra' narrated from his father, and Ahmad ibn Yazid al-Sulami, read ﴿and that they may be warned﴾ with a *ya'* and *dhal* vowelled as the imperfect of *nadhara bi-l-shay'*, meaning "he knew of the thing and so prepared for it." They said: no verbal noun is known for *nadhara* in the sense of "knew," so it is like *'asa* and other verbs that have no verbal nouns. It is also said that they dispensed with the pure verbal noun by using *an* with the verb. In the Qamus: *nadhira bi-l-shay'* (like *fariha*) means he knew it and so took precaution against it; and *andhara-hu bi-l-amr* (warned him of the matter), *indhaaran, nadharan, and nadhiran*, meaning he informed him of it and warned him.

Mujahid and Humayd read with a *ta'* vowelled with a *damma* and a *dhal* vowelled with a *kasra*: ﴿and that they may know﴾, by looking and reflecting upon what is in it of clear proofs, which are the destruction of nations and the settling of others in their dwellings, and other things included in what it indicated: ﴿that He is only one God﴾, having no partner at all. The warning is placed first because it leads to reflection, which entails the knowledge mentioned. ﴿And that those of understanding may be reminded﴾. (52) That is, that they may remember the affairs of God, exalted is He, and His dealings with His servants and similar things, and so refrain from the qualities by which the disbelievers are characterized, which would ruin them, and clothe themselves with what brings them favour in His presence, mighty and majestic is He, from sound beliefs and righteous deeds. In restricting the remembrance to those of understanding there is an elevation of their rank.

In Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim it is said that in this there is an allusion to the knowledge being specific to the disbelievers, and an indication that what is referred to by "this" is the calamities directed at their affairs, not the whole surah that contains them and what is addressed to the believers as well, for in it there is a new benefit for them, and there is room for discussion about it. Also in it: since what the message conveys of monotheism and what follows from it of rulings is a new matter in relation to the disbelievers, and for those of understanding, perseverance in that, he expressed the first by knowledge and the second by remembrance. The order of existence was observed, [p. 259] together with what is in it of closing with the most beautiful.

The judge (al-Qadi, Baydawi) — may God whiten the brow of his states — mentioned that He, glory be to Him, mentioned three benefits for this message, which are the goal and the wisdom in sending down the books: the perfecting of the Messengers, upon them be peace, for mankind, which is referred to by the warning; and the completion of their theoretical faculty, whose ultimate perfection is what relates to the knowledge of God, exalted is He, referred to by "knowledge"; and the rectifying of the practical faculty, which is clothing oneself with the garment of piety, referred to by "remembrance." The apparent meaning is that by "those of understanding" is meant the people of pure intellects, free of the impurities of illusion in every respect. It does not detract from this what has been said: that the verse was revealed concerning Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, and the end of this surah corresponds to its beginning. This is frequent in the surahs of the Qur'an, to the point that some claimed that His words, exalted is He: ﴿and that they may be warned by it﴾ are conjoined to His words, glory be to Him: ﴿to bring mankind out﴾; and that is at a remove that we ask Him, glory be to Him, mighty and majestic is He, to bestow upon us showers of pardon and forgiveness.

* * *

This (and from the door of allusion in the verses):

﴿And when Abraham said: My Lord, make this city secure﴾. Ibn 'Ata said: Abraham, upon him be peace, meant that He, glory be to Him, should make his heart secure from separation and veiling. It is said: make the city of my heart secure through You, from You. ﴿And keep me and my sons far from worshipping idols﴾, from base desires and sensory longings.

Ja'far, may God be pleased with him, said: he, upon him be peace, meant: do not return me to witnessing the intimate friendship (khullah), nor return my sons to witnessing prophethood. He also said: the idols of intimate friendship are the thoughts of heedlessness and the glances of love. In another narration, he, upon him be peace, was secure from worshipping idols in his old age, though he had broken them in his youth; but he knew that every person's desire is his idol, so he sought refuge from that.

Al-Junayd, may his secret be sanctified, said: meaning, keep me and my sons from seeking for ourselves a means to You other than dependence. It is said: whatever the knower stops at other than the Truth, glory be to Him, is his idol, and the self is the greatest idol. ﴿My Lord, they have led many of mankind astray﴾, by attachment to them, being drawn to them, and veiling oneself by them from You, glory be to You. ﴿So whoever follows me﴾ on the path of striving and intimate friendship, by giving up the spirit before You, ﴿then he is of me﴾: his clay is from my clay, his heart from my heart, his spirit from my spirit, his secret from my secret, and his drinking-place in intimate friendship is from my drinking-place. ﴿And whoever disobeys me﴾ and does what requires veiling from You, ﴿then indeed You are Forgiving, Merciful﴾; so I do not invoke against him, and I entrust his affair to You. It is said that this from him, upon him be peace, is a supplication for the disobedient, that God, exalted is He, cover his darkness with His light and His mercy, mighty is His majesty, and bestow upon him the perfection after forgiveness. And among the words of our Prophet, may God's blessings and peace be upon him, is: "O God, guide my people, for they do not know."

In Asrar al-Ta'wil it is said that he, upon him be peace, by his words ﴿And whoever disobeys me﴾ alluded to the station of unification (jam'), and for this reason he did not say: "whoever disobeys You." It is also permissible to say: he attributed their disobedience to himself only because the disobedience of creatures against the Creator is not possible: ﴿There is no creature but that He holds its forelock﴾, so they are in all their states responding to the call of the tongues of His will, glory be to Him, and His eternal decree. 'Abd al-'Aziz al-Makki was asked why al-Khalil did not say: "whoever disobeys You," and he said: because he magnified his Lord, mighty and majestic is He, and glorified Him beyond establishing that anyone would dare to disobey Him, glory be to Him. Likewise he glorified Him, glory be to Him, beyond anyone reaching the level befitting His majesty of obedience to Him, when he said: ﴿So whoever follows me﴾.

﴿Our Lord, I have settled some of my offspring in an uncultivated valley near Your Sacred House﴾. It is said that it is among God's customs, exalted is He, to test His intimate friend with great matters, so as to strip him of himself and of the whole creation, lest any veil of temporality remain between him and Him. For this reason, mighty is His majesty, He commanded this intimate friend to settle some of his offspring in the valley of the Sanctuary without water or provision, so that he would be cut off towards Him and rely on none but Him, mighty and majestic is He. He called Him by the name "Lord," hoping that He would nurture his family and dependents with His kindnesses and shelter them in the neighbourhood of His honour. ﴿Our Lord, that they may establish prayer﴾, by which the servant reaches You and which becomes a mirror of Your manifestation. ﴿So make hearts from among the people incline towards them﴾, leaning with the quality of will and love, so that they may guide them to You and point them to You. Ibn 'Ata said: whoever cuts himself off from creatures entirely, God, exalted is He, turns the faces of creatures towards him and places his affection in their breasts and his love in their hearts. That is from the supplication of the intimate friend, upon him be peace, when he cut his family off from creatures and means, and said: ﴿So make hearts from among the people incline towards them, and provide them with fruits﴾. It is said: meaning the fruits of Your obedience, which are the lofty stations and the noble degrees.

Al-Wasiti said: the fruits of the hearts, which are kinds of wisdom. The chief of wisdom is seeing the favour and being unable to give thanks for the blessing, and this is true gratitude; for this reason He said: ﴿so that they may give thanks﴾, meaning, they know that it is not possible for anyone to fulfil Your thanks. The fruit of wisdom removes the diseases from the hearts, just as the fruit of trees removes the diseases of souls. It is also said: meaning, provide them with children who are prophets and righteous, and in this there is an allusion to his supplication for the Master of the Messengers, may God's blessings and peace be upon him, which was granted to him in His words: ﴿Our Lord, and raise up among them a Messenger﴾. And which fruits are more desirable than the purest of the pure, the most pious of the pious, the most excellent of the people of earth and heaven, and the beloved of the Lord of Greatness and Majesty? He, upon him be blessings and peace, is the fruit of the Abrahamic tree and the flower of the gardens of the Khalilic call. Indeed, he, may God bless him, is the fruit of the tree of existence, the light of the garden of generosity and bounty, and the light of the pupil of every existent, upon him be blessings until the Day that is witnessed.

﴿Our Lord, You know what we conceal and what we reveal﴾. Al-Khawwas said: what we conceal of Your love, and what we reveal of Your thanks.

Ibn 'Ata said: what we conceal of states, and what we reveal of courtesies. It is said: what we conceal of humility in Your servitude, and what we reveal of the outward obedience to Your law. And also: what we conceal of the secrets of Your knowledge, and what we reveal of the duties of Your worship. And also: what we conceal of the realities of longing for You in our hearts, and what we reveal in the overwhelming of our ecstasies by the flowing of tears and the sending up of sighs:

Alas for the lovers, they strive to hide love and passion, but the telltale betrays them.
If they reveal the secret, their blood is shed, and so is the blood of those who reveal it.
And if they conceal it, the flowing tear tells of them to the slanderers.

And al-Sayyid 'Ali al-Bandanijji, may his secret be sanctified, said:

I concealed the passion for His love out of fear of disclosure; how many a lover has been harmed by the disclosure!
But its traces appeared from my groaning; when musk spreads its scent, how can its fragrance stay hidden?

﴿Nothing is hidden from God in the earth or in the heaven﴾, so He knows what is hidden and what is manifest. ﴿And do not think that God is unaware of what the wrongdoers do. He only defers them to a Day when eyes will stare﴾. It is said: the wrongdoer is one who oversteps his bounds and struts upon the carpet of selfhood, claiming that he has drunk deeply from the water of Zamzam of love and has been immersed in the deep sea of annihilation (fana'). God, exalted is He, threatened him that his disgrace would be deferred until a Day when the eyes of the intoxicated by gnosis and unity (tawhid) will stare, and that is the Day of the Greatest Unveiling, when the lights of the majesty of might appear, so that they are absorbed in His greatness, to the point that they cannot turn to anything else. There the truthful is distinguished from the liar:

When tears mingle upon cheeks, it becomes clear who weeps from among those who pretend to weep.

His words, glory be to Him: ﴿Hastening forward, heads raised, their gaze does not return to them, and their hearts are void﴾ describe the states of those whose eyes stare, and they are truly the intoxicated by love. Ibn 'Ata said concerning ﴿and their hearts are void﴾: this is the description of the hearts of the people of the Truth, attached to God, exalted is He; they are at rest only with Him, glory be to Him, they are calm only towards Him, and there is no room in them for anyone else. ﴿And warn mankind of the Day when the punishment will come to them, and those who did wrong will say: Our Lord, delay us for a short term, we will answer Your call and follow the Messengers﴾. They sought to make up for what had passed, by refining the inner and outer and joining the path of the truthful; but far off, far off indeed! Then they were answered with what breaks the back and tears away the sight of the eyes, which is His words, glory be to Him: ﴿Did you not swear before that you would not depart?﴾ and the verse.

Commentary of al-Alusi (Ruh al-Ma'ani) on surah 14, verse 52 (part 2 of 2):

﴿The day the earth will be changed to another earth, and the heavens [as well], and they will come forth before Allah, the One, the Subduer.﴾ This is at the unveiling of the lights of the reality of existence, so the destruction of everything becomes manifest except His Face.

It has been said: the allusion in the verse is to the transformation of the earth of the hearts of the gnostics from the attributes of humanity to the sacred spiritual attributes, by the light of witnessing the beauty of the Real, and the transformation of the heavens of the spirits from the weakness and incapacity of the attributes of contingency, by the outpouring of the true attributes upon the lights of majesty. It has also been said: the earth of nature is changed into the earth of the self upon reaching the station of the heart, and the heaven of the heart into the heaven of the innermost secret (sirr), and likewise the earth of the self is changed into the earth of the heart, and the heaven of the secret into the heaven of the spirit. Likewise, every station the wayfarer passes through, what is above it and what is below it is changed, like the change of the heaven of trust (tawakkul) in the unity of actions into the heaven of contentment (rida) in the unity of attributes, then the heaven of contentment into the heaven of unity at the unveiling of the Essence. ﴿And you will see the criminals that Day bound together in shackles﴾, bound with the chains of desires. ﴿Their garments will be of pitch﴾, which is the pitch of their foul deeds. ﴿And the Fire will cover﴾, i.e., will conceal, ﴿their faces﴾ in the Hell of deprivation, the blazing fire of humiliation and of being veiled from the Lord of lords.

﴿This is a message for mankind, that they may be warned thereby, and that they may know that He is but one God, and that those of understanding may take heed﴾. And they are the scholars of reality, the pillars of gnosis, the lovers of the Presence, and the trustees of the treasuries of the kingdom. May Allah Most High make us and you among those who are reminded and so remember, and who are established and confirmed in the abode of unity, by His grace and generosity, glory be to Him.
